action: 2 critical OT exposure(s); remediate via the network path, not a device change: Introduce a segmentation boundary (firewall/data diode) in the next window; Change credentials in a planned window; compensate with access control now. All OT changes require safety review plus CISO and operations-director approval.
rationale: Each finding is scored for OT: an IT/OT bridge or an internet-exposed device removes the containment boundary and is critical, as are default credentials on a safety-critical device. Remediation favours network-path changes over device changes because OT prioritises availability and safety; every mutating OT action requires safety review plus CISO and operations-director approval. Read-only assessment.
key_findings: 3 device(s): 6 finding(s) (2 critical, 2 high); OT paradox — availability and safety before patching
critical hmi-line-3 (Purdue 2, s7, safety-critical): IT/OT network bridge — removes the primary OT containment boundary -> Introduce a segmentation boundary (firewall/data diode) in the next window
critical hmi-line-3 (Purdue 2, s7, safety-critical): default credentials on an OT device -> Change credentials in a planned window; compensate with access control now
high plc-boiler (Purdue 1, modbus, safety-critical): unpatchable legacy device -> Wrap in compensating controls (segmentation, monitoring); do not force-patch
high cam-gate (Purdue 3, other): flat OT network with no zone segmentation -> Segment per the Purdue model / IEC 62443 zones
medium plc-boiler (Purdue 1, modbus, safety-critical): plaintext OT protocol -> Add network monitoring; encrypt where the device supports it
medium cam-gate (Purdue 3, other): no passive OT network monitoring -> Deploy passive OT IDS (no active scanning of OT)
